strategies.title: Funding basis
strategies.description:
Holds the spot asset and shorts the perpetual against it, so the position has no view on the price, and collects the funding the shorts are paid while the perpetual trades above the spot. When funding falls far enough it unwinds, and when the vault falls far enough from its peak it only reduces.

The edge is mechanical and it compresses as more capital chases it, which is the honest thing to say about it: the record shows the size it was earned at, and a larger vault should expect less.
claims: Gross exposure at most twice the vault's value
No single order above 5% of the vault
6% of the vault kept liquid, so an ordinary withdrawal closes nothing
Only reduces after a 10% fall from the vault's peak
One market, BTC against BTC-PERP, and nothing else
strategies.author: shonin

[workspace]
resolver = "3"
members = ["packages/agents/funding-basis"]

[workspace.package]
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.98"
license = "Apache-2.0"
publish = false

[workspace.dependencies]
# The SDK an agent is written against. It is declared by version, and a
# local checkout is patched in through .cargo/config.toml while both move
# together; the build service supplies its own pinned copy the same way, so
# `--locked` holds on both sides.
shonin-strategy-sdk = "0.1.0"

futures = "0.3.34"
serde = { version = "1.0.229", features = ["derive"] }

[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "deny"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }

[profile.release]
# An agent is a component the build service compiles from source with a
# pinned recipe, so the profile is part of what makes it reproducible.
opt-level = "s"
lto = true
codegen-units = 1
strip = true

[package]
name = "funding-basis"
description = "Holds spot, shorts the perp, and collects the funding between them"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
rust-version.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
publish.workspace = true

[lib]

[dependencies]

[lints]
workspace = true

[vault]
chain = "base"

[description]
title = "Funding basis"
text = """
Holds the spot asset and shorts the perpetual against it, so the position has \
no view on the price, and collects the funding the shorts are paid while the \
perpetual trades above the spot. When funding falls far enough it unwinds, \
and when the vault falls far enough from its peak it only reduces.

The edge is mechanical and it compresses as more capital chases it, which is \
the honest thing to say about it: the record shows the size it was earned at, \
and a larger vault should expect less.
"""
claims = [
    "Gross exposure at most twice the vault's value",
    "No single order above 5% of the vault",
    "6% of the vault kept liquid, so an ordinary withdrawal closes nothing",
    "Only reduces after a 10% fall from the vault's peak",
    "One market, BTC against BTC-PERP, and nothing else",
]

[drivers.local]

# Pinned to an exact stable release so every machine and the reproducible
# executor image build with the same compiler. Bump deliberately.
[toolchain]
channel = "1.98.1"
components = ["rustfmt", "clippy"]
targets = ["wasm32-unknown-unknown", "wasm32-wasip2"]

legs.key: an agent the vault's station approved, trade-only
cannot: send a dollar anywhere but the vault's own accounts

findings.summary: The drawdown-stop's high-water mark lives only in process memory and resets to zero on every restart, so a redeploy or crash during a drawdown silently re-arms the strategy to open new risk instead of staying in reduce-only mode.
findings.detail: The vault peaks at $1,000,000, falls to $880,000 (12% off peak), and the agent correctly enters reduce-only mode. The process is then restarted (a routine deploy, an orchestration restart, a crash). `Mind::new()` sets `peak = zero()` (lib.rs:87), and the first `step()` call sets `peak` to the current $880,000 (lib.rs:155-157) instead of the true $1,000,000 high-water mark. `only_reducing` (lib.rs:93-95) now compares against the wrong, lower peak, finds no 10% drawdown, and the agent resumes opening new carry positions at a vault level that a depositor was told would only be reduced.

findings.summary: The gross-leverage and per-order ceilings on the position-opening path are enforced entirely inside the external, unreviewed `size_for` function from `shonin-strategy-sdk`, so no ceiling for that path is actually visible in the submitted source.
findings.detail: `open_one_step` computes a desired notional and hands it, along with `mind.limits`, to `size_for` (lib.rs:202-208) without any further check on the returned value before using it to size both legs. Only the unwind path has a visible, self-contained cap (`cap_by_notional`, lib.rs:349-355). If the SDK's `size_for` ever fails to honor `max_gross_leverage` or `max_order_fraction` for some input combination, nothing in this project would catch it before the order is placed.

findings.summary: The per-order `Verdict`s returned by the venue are discarded unchecked, so a partial fill across the paired spot/perp legs (one leg filled, the other rejected) would not be detected or specifically corrected.
findings.detail: `open_one_step` submits a spot buy and a perp sell together and relies on the comment's assumption that 'the venue answers for both together,' but then calls `.map(|_| ())` on the result (lib.rs:260), throwing away the `Vec<Verdict>`. `submit` itself (lib.rs:360-363) never inspects or surfaces per-action failures either. If the venue ever fills one leg and rejects the other, the code has no leg-mismatch detection: the next `step()` just tries to add more paired exposure toward `target_deployment`, leaving the stray naked leg from the failed submission unaddressed indefinitely.

findings.summary: The test meant to prove 'the claims in the manifest are the limits in the code' is itself stale and checks for values that don't match either the manifest or the config, so it would fail if run.
findings.detail: `the_manifest_claims_the_limits_the_code_keeps` asserts `manifest.contains("5% of the vault kept liquid") && config::IDLE_BUFFER == "0.05"` (lib.rs:398). The actual `shonin.toml` says '6% of the vault kept liquid' and `config::IDLE_BUFFER` is `"0.06"` (config.rs:26). The assertion is `false && false`, so `cargo test` would fail on this case. The mechanism the module doc (lib.rs:14-17) and this test advertise as the guarantee that 'a depositor reading the page and a reviewer reading the source are looking at the same promises' is not actually working, even though the real values happen to agree.

findings.summary: Gross exposure is computed by defaulting an unpriced position's mark to zero rather than failing safe, which would silently understate deployed capital if market data for a held position is briefly unavailable.
findings.detail: `gross_notional` looks up `state.market(&held.market)` and falls back to `unwrap_or_else(zero)` for the price if the market isn't currently listed in venue state (lib.rs:332-336). If that ever happens transiently for an open position, `gross` is undercounted, `wanted = working - gross` is overstated, and `open_one_step` would add more exposure than the target-deployment logic intends, rather than pausing until fresh data is available.

review.summary: The agent runs one long-lived loop (`FundingBasis::run`) that reacts to venue account events and vault events rather than polling. On each wake it reads account state, and if BTC-PERP funding is at or above an entry threshold and the vault isn't in a drawdown, it tops up a spot-long/perp-short pair toward a target fraction of the vault's value (both legs submitted together, sized through an external SDK helper `size_for` against configured limits). If funding falls below an exit threshold, or the vault has fallen 10% from its tracked peak, it unwinds one bounded step at a time (perp leg first, then spot, each capped at a fraction of vault value via a self-contained `cap_by_notional`). On a vault halt signal it flattens the book in bounded reduce-only steps, falling back to the vault contract's own close path if it can't finish within 32 iterations. Vault buffer shortfalls pull cash back from the venue on a best-effort basis. All limits (gross leverage 2x, 5% per order, 6% idle buffer, 10% drawdown stop) live as named constants in config.rs that mirror the shonin.toml claims in wording, with a test intended to keep the two in sync — a test that, as shown above, is itself out of date.
limits: The strategy-sdk crate (`shonin-strategy-sdk`) is an external dependency patched in via a `.cargo/config.toml` not included in this submission. Its implementation of `size_for`, `Limits` enforcement, `Order`/`Verdict` semantics, `drivers::submit` (including whether multiple actions in one call are atomic), `vault::events`, and `transfers::move_` could not be read, so several of the claimed ceilings and the all-or-nothing assumption behind paired order submission could not be verified against actual enforcement code.
The 'local' driver referenced by `[drivers.local]` in shonin.toml, and the venue/market data it exposes (prices, funding, fills), are not part of the submitted source and could not be inspected.

No Cargo.lock was provided, so the exact resolved and pinned version of `shonin-strategy-sdk` and other dependencies could not be confirmed, limiting how far the reproducibility claim built on `--locked` could be checked.

This review is a static reading of the submitted source only; it cannot observe runtime behavior (actual fills, funding payment timing, venue outages or rate limits) and is one reading of the code, not a proof that it is safe or free of defects.

strategies.title: Funding basis, retired
strategies.description:
Holds the spot asset and shorts the perpetual against it, so the position has no view on the price, and collects the funding the shorts are paid while the perpetual trades above the spot. When funding falls far enough it unwinds, and when the vault falls far enough from its peak it only reduces.

The edge is mechanical and it compresses as more capital chases it, which is the honest thing to say about it: the record shows the size it was earned at, and a larger vault should expect less.
claims: Gross exposure at most twice the vault's value
No single order above 5% of the vault
6% of the vault kept liquid, so an ordinary withdrawal closes nothing
Only reduces after a 10% fall from the vault's peak
One market, BTC against BTC-PERP, and nothing else

findings.summary: The drawdown-stop's high-water mark lives only in process memory and resets to zero on every restart, silently disabling the claimed 10% drawdown protection.
findings.detail: The vault peaks at $1,000,000, falls to $850,000 (15% down, past the claimed 10% stop), and the agent process restarts (deploy, crash, host replacement) before falling further. Mind::new() sets peak = 0, and the very first step() call sets peak = current vault_value ($850,000). only_reducing() now measures drawdown from $850,000, not the true $1,000,000 peak, so the agent resumes opening new carry positions even though it is already well past the stated 10% stop, until it falls another 10% from the restart point.

findings.summary: submit() discards the per-action Verdicts from a two-leg order, so a rejected leg leaves the agent silently holding the unhedged side.
findings.detail: open_one_step submits a spot buy and a perp sell as two separate Actions in one call (lib.rs:243-260); submit() maps the result to () and the caller never inspects it (lib.rs:360-363). If the venue fills the spot buy but rejects the perp sell (margin check, price-band reject, etc.), the next step() sees position(spot) > 0 and position(perp) == 0, so `carrying` is false and the unwind branch never fires; the directional spot exposure the strategy exists to avoid is never explicitly closed, only diluted by future target-deployment math.

findings.summary: flatten() raises max_order_fraction to 100% of the vault, contradicting the unconditional manifest claim "No single order above 5% of the vault."
findings.detail: A depositor reading the claims list sees an unqualified 5%-per-order ceiling. During a halt, flatten() overrides limits.max_order_fraction to Decimal::from(1) before calling unwind_one_step, so a single closing order can be sized up to the entire vault's notional. The code's rationale (avoid stranding a leg during a halt) is reasonable, but the claims text carries no exception for this case, so the stated limit is not actually a limit in the one situation where order size could spike the most.

findings.summary: The test meant to prove the manifest's claims match the code's constants is itself wrong: it checks for "5% of the vault kept liquid" and IDLE_BUFFER == "0.05", but the manifest says 6% and config.rs sets IDLE_BUFFER to "0.06".
findings.detail: Running `cargo test` on this exact source fails: shonin.toml (line 19) reads "6% of the vault kept liquid" and config.rs (line 26) defines IDLE_BUFFER = "0.06", while the assertion at lib.rs:398 looks for the substring "5% of the vault kept liquid" and compares IDLE_BUFFER to "0.05". The one test whose job is to guarantee the claims and the code stay in step is stale, so a reader cannot rely on "the tests pass" as evidence the other four claims it checks are still accurate either.

findings.summary: The two limits most directly bounding risk size, gross leverage and the open-path per-order cap, are enforced inside size_for() in the shonin-strategy-sdk crate, which is not part of the submitted source.
findings.detail: Not a concrete failure so much as a verification gap: unlike the drawdown stop, idle buffer, and the unwind-path cap_by_notional (all implemented and readable in this file), the open path's sizing passes wanted/vault_value/gross/limits/minimum_notional into an external function the reviewer cannot read. In this agent's own logic, target_deployment (0.80) keeps intended gross well under the claimed 2x ceiling, so the ceiling is unlikely to bind in normal operation, but whether size_for would actually clamp an order correctly if it did bind cannot be confirmed from this code alone.

review.summary: A single-strategy Rust crate (funding-basis) built against a strategy SDK: it holds spot BTC and shorts BTC-PERP in equal notional, opening more of the pair when funding is rich and unwinding it (perp leg first) when funding falls below a threshold or the vault has dropped 10% from a peak it tracks in memory. Position sizing targets 80% of vault value deployed, is nudged forward one bounded step at a time on every venue or vault event, moves only the needed cash from vault to venue while preserving a 6% idle buffer, and on a halt event flattens everything with its order-size cap lifted. The code is small, readable, and mostly matches its own stated claims, but two mechanisms undercut them in ways a careful reader would flag: the drawdown-stop's high-water mark is never restored from anything external after a restart, and two-leg order submissions do not check per-leg success, so a rejected fill is not distinguished from an accepted one.
limits: The shonin-strategy-sdk crate (size_for, Limits, drivers::*, vault::*, transfers::*) is an external dependency and not part of the submitted source, so the real enforcement of the gross-leverage and open-path order-size claims, and whether a multi-action submit() call is atomic or settles each leg independently, cannot be verified directly.
The .cargo/config.toml patch referenced in the root Cargo.toml comment, which pins the SDK to a specific checkout, was not supplied.

config/drivers.toml and whatever venue the manifest's "local" driver actually resolves to were not supplied, so the real liquidity and manipulability of the traded BTC / BTC-PERP market cannot be assessed from this source.
No backtest, runtime log, or live trading history was supplied; this review is one static reading of the source and is not a proof of how the agent behaves once deployed.
Whether the shonin-strategy-sdk crate itself has build scripts or procedural macros that could affect reproducibility was not visible from this project's files.

findings.summary: The drawdown-stop's 'peak' is kept only in the process's memory and is reseeded from the current vault value on every restart, so a restart during a drawdown silently erases how far the vault has already fallen.
findings.detail: The vault falls 12% from its true peak, past the 10% drawdown stop, so the agent should only be reducing. The process restarts (a deploy, a crash, a host replacement). `Mind::new()` sets `peak = zero()` (lib.rs:87); the first `step()` call sees `state.vault_value > mind.peak` and sets `peak` to the current, already-depressed value (lib.rs:155-157). `only_reducing` (lib.rs:93-95) now compares the vault against this new, lower peak instead of the real one, finds no 10% fall from it, and the agent resumes opening new carry positions exactly when it should be flattening. The module doc at lib.rs:38-39 claims restarting 'costs a moment and nothing else,' which is true for positions (rebuilt from the venue) but false for this specific piece of state.

findings.summary: Opening a carry step submits the spot buy and perp sell as one batch and then discards the per-order result, so a leg that fails to fill is never detected or corrected by the agent itself.
findings.detail: `open_one_step` submits both orders together and the comment (lib.rs:240-242) argues this is safe because 'the venue answers for both together,' but `submit()` (lib.rs:360-363) returns the `Vec<Verdict>` and every call site discards it with `.map(|_| ())` (lib.rs:259-261, lib.rs:302). If the spot buy fills and the perp sell is rejected (a venue-side margin check, a stale quote, a partial book), the agent is left long spot with no hedge — precisely the directional bet the strategy says it never means to hold. `unwind_one_step` only triggers once `carrying` is true (spot long AND perp short, lib.rs:170-171), so a naked spot-only position is not targeted by the reduce path and is only closed out later if a full `Halting`/`flatten()` occurs. Until then the stray exposure is uncapped in duration and unremediated by this code.

findings.summary: The two headline risk claims most likely to matter to a depositor — 'gross exposure at most twice the vault' and 'no single order above 5%' on the opening path — are enforced entirely inside `size_for`, a function from `shonin-strategy-sdk` that is not part of the submitted source.
findings.detail: `open_one_step` computes `wanted` and then hands it, together with `mind.limits` (built from the config constants), to `size_for(...)` (lib.rs:202-208) with no further check in this file on the value it returns. Unlike the reduce path, which clamps locally with `cap_by_notional` (lib.rs:349-355, using `max_order_fraction` directly), the open path has no agent-level ceiling at all — if `size_for` had a bug or a different interpretation of `Limits` than the author intends, nothing in this project would catch an order or a gross exposure that exceeds the claimed caps. A reviewer reading only this source cannot confirm the two leverage/size claims hold for opens; they can only confirm the right numbers are passed in.

findings.summary: The self-test meant to prove the manifest's claims match the code's constants is itself stale: it checks for '5% of the vault kept liquid' and `IDLE_BUFFER == "0.05"`, but the manifest actually says 6% and `config::IDLE_BUFFER` is `"0.06"` — so this test would fail as shipped.
findings.detail: `shonin.toml:19` reads '6% of the vault kept liquid,' and `config.rs:26` sets `IDLE_BUFFER = "0.06"`, matching each other correctly. But `lib.rs:398`'s assertion `manifest.contains("5% of the vault kept liquid") && config::IDLE_BUFFER == "0.05"` tests for the old 5% figure on both sides and would not pass against the current manifest text or constant, meaning `the_manifest_claims_the_limits_the_code_keeps` does not actually verify what its name promises for this one limit — the claims-equal-code invariant for the idle buffer is currently unverified by the test suite, even though the claim and the enforcing code (lib.rs:216-221) happen to still agree with each other.

review.summary: The project is a single Rust agent (`funding-basis`) built against `shonin-strategy-sdk`. It runs as one long-lived async loop woken by venue account events and vault events. On each wake it reads account state, checks the perpetual's funding rate, and either opens one more step of a delta-neutral carry (long BTC spot, short BTC-PERP, both legs submitted in one batch) when funding is rich enough and the vault isn't in a drawdown, or unwinds one step (perp first, then spot, each capped by `max_order_fraction`) when funding has fallen below the exit threshold or the vault has dropped `DRAWDOWN_STOP` (10%) from its in-memory peak. A separate halt path (`flatten`) closes everything without the per-order cap when the vault signals it is stopping. The five claims in `shonin.toml` map directly to five constants in `config.rs`, and most of them are enforced by code in this file; the opening path's leverage and per-order caps, however, are delegated to an SDK function (`size_for`) not included in the submission. I found two reliability issues worth a careful reader's attention — the drawdown-stop's 'peak' does not survive a restart, and a failed fill on one leg of a paired spot/perp order is not detected or corrected by this code — plus one place where the open-path risk claims aren't verifiable from the given source, and one stale self-test that no longer matches the manifest it is meant to check against.
limits: The strategy SDK (`shonin-strategy-sdk`) is not part of the submitted source: `Account`, `VenueAccount`, `Decimal`, `Limits`, `Order`, `Verdict`, `size_for`, `millionths`, and the `drivers`/`vault`/`transfers` modules are all opaque. Every claim that depends on how `size_for` actually bounds an order, how `drivers::submit` sequences or guarantees atomicity between the two legs, or how `AccountState`/`vault::VaultEvent` are populated, could not be checked against real logic — only against how this crate calls them.

The actual venue/exchange behind the 'local' driver (its liquidity for BTC/BTC-PERP, fee schedule, order-rejection behavior, and whether it fills paired orders atomically) is not in the submitted project, so manipulable-markets and reliability-under-venue-error could only be judged from the agent's own assumptions about it, not from the venue itself.
No `Cargo.lock` was included, so the exact resolved dependency graph (and therefore full build reproducibility) could not be confirmed, only the version constraints in `Cargo.toml`.

This is a static reading of source with no weights, live data, or execution: nothing here was run, so behavior under real funding rates, prices, or venue responses is inferred from the code, not observed.
A review is one reading of the code at one point in time, not a proof that these are the only issues or that the issues found will manifest in practice.

findings.summary: A rejected or partial fill on one leg of the paired spot/perp order can leave the agent holding a naked directional position that neither the opening path nor the unwind path is built to detect or close.
findings.detail: open_one_step (lib.rs:188-261) submits a spot buy and a perp sell together via one submit() call, but drivers::submit returns a Vec<Verdict> — one verdict per action — so the two legs can fill independently. step() (lib.rs:169-181) only recognizes an open carry when `state.position(spot) > 0 && state.position(perp) < 0` (the `carrying` flag, lines 170-171). If only one leg fills, `carrying` is false, so unwind_one_step is never reached from the normal loop (it is only called unconditionally during flatten() on a Halting event, lib.rs:308-325). The lone leg then sits as uncorrected directional exposure unless a later funding-driven open_one_step call happens to add the missing leg back in roughly the right size — which is not guaranteed, since that path sizes off `wanted = target_deployment*vault_value - gross`, not off the specific shortfall. This directly contradicts the design claim that the position 'has no view on the price.'

findings.summary: The drawdown-stop's high-water mark lives only in memory and resets to the current vault value on every process restart, quietly widening the risk window the 10% claim is supposed to bound.
findings.detail: Mind::peak (lib.rs:40-46) starts at zero() in Mind::new() (line 87) and is first set to the current vault_value the moment step() runs after a restart (lines 155-157), because zero() is always less than a positive value. If the vault previously ran up and then fell, a restart (crash, redeploy, venue disconnect) erases the memory of that earlier peak; only_reducing() (lines 93-95) then measures the 10% drawdown stop from the new, lower post-restart peak instead of the vault's true historical peak. The field's own doc comment ('the most the vault has been worth while this instance watched it') shows this is an intentional scope, but it is narrower than the manifest's unqualified claim 'a 10% fall from the vault's peak,' and the Mind struct's top-level comment ('losing it to a restart costs a moment and nothing else') does not hold for this field.

findings.summary: The embedded test that checks the manifest's claims against the code's constants is itself stale: it checks for a 5% idle-buffer figure that matches neither the shipped 6% manifest text nor the 0.06 constant.
findings.detail: the_manifest_claims_the_limits_the_code_keeps (lib.rs:390-401) asserts `manifest.contains("5% of the vault kept liquid") && config::IDLE_BUFFER == "0.05"` (line 398). The actual shonin.toml says 'kept liquid' at 6%, and config.rs:26 sets IDLE_BUFFER to "0.06" (with a comment explaining it was deliberately raised above the vault's own 5% idle floor). As written this assertion is false on both sides and the test would fail, meaning the author's own 'claims equal code' self-check was not kept in sync with the IDLE_BUFFER bump. The real enforcement at lib.rs:216-221 does correctly use 0.06, so runtime behavior matches the manifest; only the self-verifying test is wrong.

review.summary: The package is a single long-running async agent (FundingBasis) that holds BTC spot long and BTC-PERP short in equal notional, widening the pair when perp funding is attractive and the vault isn't in drawdown, and unwinding it when funding falls or the vault has dropped 10% from its peak. Every event (a venue account update or a vault event) triggers one `step()`: read fresh state from the venue, decide to open, unwind, or do nothing, and submit at most one paired order per step. Hard caps (gross leverage, per-order size, idle buffer, drawdown stop) are declared as constants in config.rs and threaded through a `Limits` struct into an SDK-provided `size_for` for opening, and into a local `cap_by_notional` for unwinding. A `Halting` vault event triggers a bounded flatten loop that ignores the per-order cap to close out before the vault's own contract-level unwind takes over."
limits: The `shonin-strategy-sdk` crate's implementation (size_for, drivers::submit/account_events/account_state, transfers::move_, vault::events, the Limits/Verdict types) is an external, versioned dependency and was not part of the submitted source, so the arithmetic that is actually supposed to enforce MAX_GROSS_LEVERAGE and MAX_ORDER_FRACTION on the opening path could not be read, only inferred from how it is called.

config/drivers.toml, which presumably defines what venue the "local" driver actually resolves to, was not shown, so the real liquidity and manipulability of the BTC / BTC-PERP market this agent trades could not be assessed directly.
The vault contract's own logic (claims, the 5% idle floor it is said never to cross, halting semantics) is referenced only through the vault:: module and was not shown.
This review did not execute the code or its test suite; the stale-test finding above is based on reading the assertion, not on an actual `cargo test` run.
Operational facts such as how often this agent process is actually restarted in production, and therefore how often the peak-reset gap would be exercised, are unknown.
This is one reading of the source, done once, and is not a proof that no other issue exists.

findings.summary: The drawdown-stop's high-water mark lives only in process memory and resets to zero on every restart, so a redeploy or crash during a drawdown silently re-arms the strategy to open new risk instead of staying in reduce-only mode.
findings.detail: The vault peaks at $1,000,000, falls to $880,000 (12% off peak), and the agent correctly enters reduce-only mode. The process is then restarted (a routine deploy, an orchestration restart, a crash). `Mind::new()` sets `peak = zero()` (lib.rs:87), and the first `step()` call sets `peak` to the current $880,000 (lib.rs:155-157) instead of the true $1,000,000 high-water mark. `only_reducing` (lib.rs:93-95) now compares against the wrong, lower peak, finds no 10% drawdown, and the agent resumes opening new carry positions at a vault level that a depositor was told would only be reduced.

findings.summary: The gross-leverage and per-order ceilings on the position-opening path are enforced entirely inside the external, unreviewed `size_for` function from `shonin-strategy-sdk`, so no ceiling for that path is actually visible in the submitted source.
findings.detail: `open_one_step` computes a desired notional and hands it, along with `mind.limits`, to `size_for` (lib.rs:202-208) without any further check on the returned value before using it to size both legs. Only the unwind path has a visible, self-contained cap (`cap_by_notional`, lib.rs:349-355). If the SDK's `size_for` ever fails to honor `max_gross_leverage` or `max_order_fraction` for some input combination, nothing in this project would catch it before the order is placed.

findings.summary: The per-order `Verdict`s returned by the venue are discarded unchecked, so a partial fill across the paired spot/perp legs (one leg filled, the other rejected) would not be detected or specifically corrected.
findings.detail: `open_one_step` submits a spot buy and a perp sell together and relies on the comment's assumption that 'the venue answers for both together,' but then calls `.map(|_| ())` on the result (lib.rs:260), throwing away the `Vec<Verdict>`. `submit` itself (lib.rs:360-363) never inspects or surfaces per-action failures either. If the venue ever fills one leg and rejects the other, the code has no leg-mismatch detection: the next `step()` just tries to add more paired exposure toward `target_deployment`, leaving the stray naked leg from the failed submission unaddressed indefinitely.

findings.summary: The test meant to prove 'the claims in the manifest are the limits in the code' is itself stale and checks for values that don't match either the manifest or the config, so it would fail if run.
findings.detail: `the_manifest_claims_the_limits_the_code_keeps` asserts `manifest.contains("5% of the vault kept liquid") && config::IDLE_BUFFER == "0.05"` (lib.rs:398). The actual `shonin.toml` says '6% of the vault kept liquid' and `config::IDLE_BUFFER` is `"0.06"` (config.rs:26). The assertion is `false && false`, so `cargo test` would fail on this case. The mechanism the module doc (lib.rs:14-17) and this test advertise as the guarantee that 'a depositor reading the page and a reviewer reading the source are looking at the same promises' is not actually working, even though the real values happen to agree.

findings.summary: Gross exposure is computed by defaulting an unpriced position's mark to zero rather than failing safe, which would silently understate deployed capital if market data for a held position is briefly unavailable.
findings.detail: `gross_notional` looks up `state.market(&held.market)` and falls back to `unwrap_or_else(zero)` for the price if the market isn't currently listed in venue state (lib.rs:332-336). If that ever happens transiently for an open position, `gross` is undercounted, `wanted = working - gross` is overstated, and `open_one_step` would add more exposure than the target-deployment logic intends, rather than pausing until fresh data is available.

review.summary: The agent runs one long-lived loop (`FundingBasis::run`) that reacts to venue account events and vault events rather than polling. On each wake it reads account state, and if BTC-PERP funding is at or above an entry threshold and the vault isn't in a drawdown, it tops up a spot-long/perp-short pair toward a target fraction of the vault's value (both legs submitted together, sized through an external SDK helper `size_for` against configured limits). If funding falls below an exit threshold, or the vault has fallen 10% from its tracked peak, it unwinds one bounded step at a time (perp leg first, then spot, each capped at a fraction of vault value via a self-contained `cap_by_notional`). On a vault halt signal it flattens the book in bounded reduce-only steps, falling back to the vault contract's own close path if it can't finish within 32 iterations. Vault buffer shortfalls pull cash back from the venue on a best-effort basis. All limits (gross leverage 2x, 5% per order, 6% idle buffer, 10% drawdown stop) live as named constants in config.rs that mirror the shonin.toml claims in wording, with a test intended to keep the two in sync — a test that, as shown above, is itself out of date.
limits: The strategy-sdk crate (`shonin-strategy-sdk`) is an external dependency patched in via a `.cargo/config.toml` not included in this submission. Its implementation of `size_for`, `Limits` enforcement, `Order`/`Verdict` semantics, `drivers::submit` (including whether multiple actions in one call are atomic), `vault::events`, and `transfers::move_` could not be read, so several of the claimed ceilings and the all-or-nothing assumption behind paired order submission could not be verified against actual enforcement code.
The 'local' driver referenced by `[drivers.local]` in shonin.toml, and the venue/market data it exposes (prices, funding, fills), are not part of the submitted source and could not be inspected.

No Cargo.lock was provided, so the exact resolved and pinned version of `shonin-strategy-sdk` and other dependencies could not be confirmed, limiting how far the reproducibility claim built on `--locked` could be checked.

This review is a static reading of the submitted source only; it cannot observe runtime behavior (actual fills, funding payment timing, venue outages or rate limits) and is one reading of the code, not a proof that it is safe or free of defects.

findings.summary: The drawdown-stop reference (`peak`) is kept only in memory and resets to zero on every restart.
findings.detail: `Mind::new()` (lib.rs:87) initializes `peak: zero()`. The very next `step()` call sets `mind.peak = state.vault_value` as soon as the current vault value exceeds this zero (lib.rs:155-157), so after any restart the drawdown-stop reference silently becomes 'the vault's value right now' instead of its true historical peak. If the vault is already deep into the 10% drawdown that is supposed to put the agent into reduce-only mode, a restart erases that memory and the agent will happily resume opening new carry positions. The struct's own doc comment (lib.rs:38-46) claims state loss on restart 'costs a moment and nothing else,' which is true for `settings` and `limits` but not for `peak` — the comment does not carve out this exception, and nothing in the code rebuilds `peak` from the venue or the vault the way it does for positions.

findings.summary: The claimed drawdown stop ('only reduces after a 10% fall from the vault's peak') is not durable across a restart.
findings.detail: shonin.toml:20 states the agent 'only reduces after a 10% fall from the vault's peak' as an unconditional behavioral claim. Because `peak` is restart-unsafe (see the paired reliability finding at lib.rs:87), this claim only holds for as long as a single process instance has been running since the vault's true peak. A restart during an active drawdown resets the reference point and the claim silently stops being true until a new, lower 'peak' has been seen and then fallen from again.

findings.summary: Per-action order results (Verdicts) are discarded at both call sites, so a rejected or partially-filled leg of the paired spot/perp order is never explicitly checked.
findings.detail: `submit()` (lib.rs:360-363) returns a `Vec<Verdict>` from the driver, one per submitted action, but both callers throw it away: `open_one_step` ends with `.map(|_| ())` (lib.rs:258-260) and `unwind_one_step` does the same (lib.rs:302). The strategy's whole safety argument for submitting both legs together is 'a filled long beside an unfilled short is a directional bet... so the venue answers for both together' (lib.rs:240-242), but the code never reads that answer. It only re-derives the picture on the next state read, and `gross_notional()` (lib.rs:328-345) sums exposure without distinguishing matched legs from unmatched ones. If one leg (e.g. the perp hedge) is repeatedly rejected while the other keeps filling, `carrying` stays false, funding still looks attractive, and `open_one_step` can be invoked again on the next event, compounding an unhedged spot position before anything in this code explicitly notices.

findings.summary: The absolute claim 'No single order above 5% of the vault' has an undisclosed exception during a halt.
findings.detail: `flatten()` builds a copy of the limits with `max_order_fraction: Decimal::from(1)` (lib.rs:309-312), i.e. 100% of the vault, and uses it for every unwind step while halting. The manifest's claim (shonin.toml:18) states the 5% per-order cap without qualification. The code's rationale (lib.rs:305-307, 322-324) — that leaving a leg on during a halt costs depositors more than a wide fill — is defensible, but it means the one hard per-order ceiling the agent advertises does not hold in exactly the stressed scenario where a large, uncapped order against a market that might be thin or moving is most costly.

findings.summary: The one test meant to prove the manifest's claims match the code's limits is itself stale and would fail if run.
findings.detail: `the_manifest_claims_the_limits_the_code_keeps` (lib.rs:390-401) asserts `manifest.contains("5% of the vault kept liquid") && config::IDLE_BUFFER == "0.05"` (lib.rs:398). The actual manifest says '6% of the vault kept liquid' (shonin.toml:19) and `config::IDLE_BUFFER` is `"0.06"` (config.rs:26) — the two agree with each other, but not with the test. This single automated check exists specifically to guarantee claims and code stay in step, and it would fail under `cargo test`/`task test` as submitted, which suggests the idle buffer was bumped from 5% to 6% without re-running the test suite before this source was published.

findings.summary: The mechanics that actually enforce the claimed limits live outside the submitted project, in the external strategy SDK.
findings.detail: `size_for(wanted, state.vault_value, gross, &mind.limits, mind.settings.minimum_notional)` (lib.rs:202-208) is where `max_gross_leverage`, `max_order_fraction` and `idle_buffer` are supposed to turn into an actual bounded order size, and `transfers::move_` (lib.rs:232-237) is where the idle-buffer floor is supposed to be respected on the vault side. Both functions are implemented in `shonin-strategy-sdk`, declared only by version in the root Cargo.toml (line 17) with a note that a local checkout is patched in during the build. Nothing in this submission shows what `size_for` or `transfers::move_` actually do, so the claims about gross leverage and the idle buffer can be checked for correct wiring in this project but not fully verified end to end from the given source alone.

findings.summary: The venue backing the 'local' driver for BTC/BTC-PERP on chain 'base' is not identified in the submission.
findings.detail: shonin.toml declares `chain = "base"` (line 2) and `[drivers.local]` (line 24) with no further parameters, and the agent code only ever refers to the market by the string constants `"BTC"` / `"BTC-PERP"` (config.rs:8-9). Whether the perpetual traded is a deep, independently-priced market or a thinner on-chain venue whose mark/funding a single party could move cheaply cannot be determined from what is given here.

review.summary: A single long-running async loop (`FundingBasis::run`) wakes on venue-account events and vault events. On each wake it reads fresh account state from the venue, and if it holds no carry and funding on BTC-PERP is rich enough, it submits a paired buy-spot/sell-perp order sized by `size_for` under four limits (gross leverage, per-order fraction, idle buffer, drawdown stop) defined as string constants in `config.rs`. If it already holds the carry and funding has fallen below the exit threshold, or the vault is down 10% from an in-memory "peak" it tracks, it submits paired reduce-only orders to unwind, capped per order by 5% of vault value. On a vault halt it flattens the whole book in up to 32 steps with the per-order cap removed. The actual arithmetic that turns the four limit constants into an order size lives in the external `shonin-strategy-sdk` crate, not in this submission.
limits: The implementation of shonin-strategy-sdk (size_for, transfers::move_, drivers::submit/account_state/account_events, vault::events, and the Limits/Verdict/Order/Action/AccountState types) was not included in the submission, so the code that actually enforces the claimed numeric limits could not be read.
Which real venue or exchange the 'local' driver connects to, its liquidity for BTC and BTC-PERP, and how its funding rate and mark price are sourced were not shown.
Whether the vault contract itself (outside this agent) independently enforces any backstop on leverage, order size, or peak-drawdown halting was not part of this submission.

This is a reading of static source only, with no live account data, market data, or test run against the actual SDK; a review of code is one reading, not a proof of how the agent will behave in production.
No separate build artifacts, CI configuration, or SDK version history were available to confirm whether the stale test noted above was ever run against this exact commit.

findings.summary: The drawdown-stop's high-water mark lives only in process memory and resets to zero on every restart, silently disabling the claimed 10% drawdown protection.
findings.detail: The vault peaks at $1,000,000, falls to $850,000 (15% down, past the claimed 10% stop), and the agent process restarts (deploy, crash, host replacement) before falling further. Mind::new() sets peak = 0, and the very first step() call sets peak = current vault_value ($850,000). only_reducing() now measures drawdown from $850,000, not the true $1,000,000 peak, so the agent resumes opening new carry positions even though it is already well past the stated 10% stop, until it falls another 10% from the restart point.

findings.summary: submit() discards the per-action Verdicts from a two-leg order, so a rejected leg leaves the agent silently holding the unhedged side.
findings.detail: open_one_step submits a spot buy and a perp sell as two separate Actions in one call (lib.rs:243-260); submit() maps the result to () and the caller never inspects it (lib.rs:360-363). If the venue fills the spot buy but rejects the perp sell (margin check, price-band reject, etc.), the next step() sees position(spot) > 0 and position(perp) == 0, so `carrying` is false and the unwind branch never fires; the directional spot exposure the strategy exists to avoid is never explicitly closed, only diluted by future target-deployment math.

findings.summary: flatten() raises max_order_fraction to 100% of the vault, contradicting the unconditional manifest claim "No single order above 5% of the vault."
findings.detail: A depositor reading the claims list sees an unqualified 5%-per-order ceiling. During a halt, flatten() overrides limits.max_order_fraction to Decimal::from(1) before calling unwind_one_step, so a single closing order can be sized up to the entire vault's notional. The code's rationale (avoid stranding a leg during a halt) is reasonable, but the claims text carries no exception for this case, so the stated limit is not actually a limit in the one situation where order size could spike the most.

findings.summary: The test meant to prove the manifest's claims match the code's constants is itself wrong: it checks for "5% of the vault kept liquid" and IDLE_BUFFER == "0.05", but the manifest says 6% and config.rs sets IDLE_BUFFER to "0.06".
findings.detail: Running `cargo test` on this exact source fails: shonin.toml (line 19) reads "6% of the vault kept liquid" and config.rs (line 26) defines IDLE_BUFFER = "0.06", while the assertion at lib.rs:398 looks for the substring "5% of the vault kept liquid" and compares IDLE_BUFFER to "0.05". The one test whose job is to guarantee the claims and the code stay in step is stale, so a reader cannot rely on "the tests pass" as evidence the other four claims it checks are still accurate either.

findings.summary: The two limits most directly bounding risk size, gross leverage and the open-path per-order cap, are enforced inside size_for() in the shonin-strategy-sdk crate, which is not part of the submitted source.
findings.detail: Not a concrete failure so much as a verification gap: unlike the drawdown stop, idle buffer, and the unwind-path cap_by_notional (all implemented and readable in this file), the open path's sizing passes wanted/vault_value/gross/limits/minimum_notional into an external function the reviewer cannot read. In this agent's own logic, target_deployment (0.80) keeps intended gross well under the claimed 2x ceiling, so the ceiling is unlikely to bind in normal operation, but whether size_for would actually clamp an order correctly if it did bind cannot be confirmed from this code alone.

review.summary: A single-strategy Rust crate (funding-basis) built against a strategy SDK: it holds spot BTC and shorts BTC-PERP in equal notional, opening more of the pair when funding is rich and unwinding it (perp leg first) when funding falls below a threshold or the vault has dropped 10% from a peak it tracks in memory. Position sizing targets 80% of vault value deployed, is nudged forward one bounded step at a time on every venue or vault event, moves only the needed cash from vault to venue while preserving a 6% idle buffer, and on a halt event flattens everything with its order-size cap lifted. The code is small, readable, and mostly matches its own stated claims, but two mechanisms undercut them in ways a careful reader would flag: the drawdown-stop's high-water mark is never restored from anything external after a restart, and two-leg order submissions do not check per-leg success, so a rejected fill is not distinguished from an accepted one.
limits: The shonin-strategy-sdk crate (size_for, Limits, drivers::*, vault::*, transfers::*) is an external dependency and not part of the submitted source, so the real enforcement of the gross-leverage and open-path order-size claims, and whether a multi-action submit() call is atomic or settles each leg independently, cannot be verified directly.
The .cargo/config.toml patch referenced in the root Cargo.toml comment, which pins the SDK to a specific checkout, was not supplied.

config/drivers.toml and whatever venue the manifest's "local" driver actually resolves to were not supplied, so the real liquidity and manipulability of the traded BTC / BTC-PERP market cannot be assessed from this source.
No backtest, runtime log, or live trading history was supplied; this review is one static reading of the source and is not a proof of how the agent behaves once deployed.
Whether the shonin-strategy-sdk crate itself has build scripts or procedural macros that could affect reproducibility was not visible from this project's files.

findings.summary: The drawdown-stop's 'peak' is kept only in the process's memory and is reseeded from the current vault value on every restart, so a restart during a drawdown silently erases how far the vault has already fallen.
findings.detail: The vault falls 12% from its true peak, past the 10% drawdown stop, so the agent should only be reducing. The process restarts (a deploy, a crash, a host replacement). `Mind::new()` sets `peak = zero()` (lib.rs:87); the first `step()` call sees `state.vault_value > mind.peak` and sets `peak` to the current, already-depressed value (lib.rs:155-157). `only_reducing` (lib.rs:93-95) now compares the vault against this new, lower peak instead of the real one, finds no 10% fall from it, and the agent resumes opening new carry positions exactly when it should be flattening. The module doc at lib.rs:38-39 claims restarting 'costs a moment and nothing else,' which is true for positions (rebuilt from the venue) but false for this specific piece of state.

findings.summary: Opening a carry step submits the spot buy and perp sell as one batch and then discards the per-order result, so a leg that fails to fill is never detected or corrected by the agent itself.
findings.detail: `open_one_step` submits both orders together and the comment (lib.rs:240-242) argues this is safe because 'the venue answers for both together,' but `submit()` (lib.rs:360-363) returns the `Vec<Verdict>` and every call site discards it with `.map(|_| ())` (lib.rs:259-261, lib.rs:302). If the spot buy fills and the perp sell is rejected (a venue-side margin check, a stale quote, a partial book), the agent is left long spot with no hedge — precisely the directional bet the strategy says it never means to hold. `unwind_one_step` only triggers once `carrying` is true (spot long AND perp short, lib.rs:170-171), so a naked spot-only position is not targeted by the reduce path and is only closed out later if a full `Halting`/`flatten()` occurs. Until then the stray exposure is uncapped in duration and unremediated by this code.

findings.summary: The two headline risk claims most likely to matter to a depositor — 'gross exposure at most twice the vault' and 'no single order above 5%' on the opening path — are enforced entirely inside `size_for`, a function from `shonin-strategy-sdk` that is not part of the submitted source.
findings.detail: `open_one_step` computes `wanted` and then hands it, together with `mind.limits` (built from the config constants), to `size_for(...)` (lib.rs:202-208) with no further check in this file on the value it returns. Unlike the reduce path, which clamps locally with `cap_by_notional` (lib.rs:349-355, using `max_order_fraction` directly), the open path has no agent-level ceiling at all — if `size_for` had a bug or a different interpretation of `Limits` than the author intends, nothing in this project would catch an order or a gross exposure that exceeds the claimed caps. A reviewer reading only this source cannot confirm the two leverage/size claims hold for opens; they can only confirm the right numbers are passed in.

findings.summary: The self-test meant to prove the manifest's claims match the code's constants is itself stale: it checks for '5% of the vault kept liquid' and `IDLE_BUFFER == "0.05"`, but the manifest actually says 6% and `config::IDLE_BUFFER` is `"0.06"` — so this test would fail as shipped.
findings.detail: `shonin.toml:19` reads '6% of the vault kept liquid,' and `config.rs:26` sets `IDLE_BUFFER = "0.06"`, matching each other correctly. But `lib.rs:398`'s assertion `manifest.contains("5% of the vault kept liquid") && config::IDLE_BUFFER == "0.05"` tests for the old 5% figure on both sides and would not pass against the current manifest text or constant, meaning `the_manifest_claims_the_limits_the_code_keeps` does not actually verify what its name promises for this one limit — the claims-equal-code invariant for the idle buffer is currently unverified by the test suite, even though the claim and the enforcing code (lib.rs:216-221) happen to still agree with each other.

review.summary: The project is a single Rust agent (`funding-basis`) built against `shonin-strategy-sdk`. It runs as one long-lived async loop woken by venue account events and vault events. On each wake it reads account state, checks the perpetual's funding rate, and either opens one more step of a delta-neutral carry (long BTC spot, short BTC-PERP, both legs submitted in one batch) when funding is rich enough and the vault isn't in a drawdown, or unwinds one step (perp first, then spot, each capped by `max_order_fraction`) when funding has fallen below the exit threshold or the vault has dropped `DRAWDOWN_STOP` (10%) from its in-memory peak. A separate halt path (`flatten`) closes everything without the per-order cap when the vault signals it is stopping. The five claims in `shonin.toml` map directly to five constants in `config.rs`, and most of them are enforced by code in this file; the opening path's leverage and per-order caps, however, are delegated to an SDK function (`size_for`) not included in the submission. I found two reliability issues worth a careful reader's attention — the drawdown-stop's 'peak' does not survive a restart, and a failed fill on one leg of a paired spot/perp order is not detected or corrected by this code — plus one place where the open-path risk claims aren't verifiable from the given source, and one stale self-test that no longer matches the manifest it is meant to check against.
limits: The strategy SDK (`shonin-strategy-sdk`) is not part of the submitted source: `Account`, `VenueAccount`, `Decimal`, `Limits`, `Order`, `Verdict`, `size_for`, `millionths`, and the `drivers`/`vault`/`transfers` modules are all opaque. Every claim that depends on how `size_for` actually bounds an order, how `drivers::submit` sequences or guarantees atomicity between the two legs, or how `AccountState`/`vault::VaultEvent` are populated, could not be checked against real logic — only against how this crate calls them.

The actual venue/exchange behind the 'local' driver (its liquidity for BTC/BTC-PERP, fee schedule, order-rejection behavior, and whether it fills paired orders atomically) is not in the submitted project, so manipulable-markets and reliability-under-venue-error could only be judged from the agent's own assumptions about it, not from the venue itself.
No `Cargo.lock` was included, so the exact resolved dependency graph (and therefore full build reproducibility) could not be confirmed, only the version constraints in `Cargo.toml`.

This is a static reading of source with no weights, live data, or execution: nothing here was run, so behavior under real funding rates, prices, or venue responses is inferred from the code, not observed.
A review is one reading of the code at one point in time, not a proof that these are the only issues or that the issues found will manifest in practice.

findings.summary: A rejected or partial fill on one leg of the paired spot/perp order can leave the agent holding a naked directional position that neither the opening path nor the unwind path is built to detect or close.
findings.detail: open_one_step (lib.rs:188-261) submits a spot buy and a perp sell together via one submit() call, but drivers::submit returns a Vec<Verdict> — one verdict per action — so the two legs can fill independently. step() (lib.rs:169-181) only recognizes an open carry when `state.position(spot) > 0 && state.position(perp) < 0` (the `carrying` flag, lines 170-171). If only one leg fills, `carrying` is false, so unwind_one_step is never reached from the normal loop (it is only called unconditionally during flatten() on a Halting event, lib.rs:308-325). The lone leg then sits as uncorrected directional exposure unless a later funding-driven open_one_step call happens to add the missing leg back in roughly the right size — which is not guaranteed, since that path sizes off `wanted = target_deployment*vault_value - gross`, not off the specific shortfall. This directly contradicts the design claim that the position 'has no view on the price.'

findings.summary: The drawdown-stop's high-water mark lives only in memory and resets to the current vault value on every process restart, quietly widening the risk window the 10% claim is supposed to bound.
findings.detail: Mind::peak (lib.rs:40-46) starts at zero() in Mind::new() (line 87) and is first set to the current vault_value the moment step() runs after a restart (lines 155-157), because zero() is always less than a positive value. If the vault previously ran up and then fell, a restart (crash, redeploy, venue disconnect) erases the memory of that earlier peak; only_reducing() (lines 93-95) then measures the 10% drawdown stop from the new, lower post-restart peak instead of the vault's true historical peak. The field's own doc comment ('the most the vault has been worth while this instance watched it') shows this is an intentional scope, but it is narrower than the manifest's unqualified claim 'a 10% fall from the vault's peak,' and the Mind struct's top-level comment ('losing it to a restart costs a moment and nothing else') does not hold for this field.

findings.summary: The embedded test that checks the manifest's claims against the code's constants is itself stale: it checks for a 5% idle-buffer figure that matches neither the shipped 6% manifest text nor the 0.06 constant.
findings.detail: the_manifest_claims_the_limits_the_code_keeps (lib.rs:390-401) asserts `manifest.contains("5% of the vault kept liquid") && config::IDLE_BUFFER == "0.05"` (line 398). The actual shonin.toml says 'kept liquid' at 6%, and config.rs:26 sets IDLE_BUFFER to "0.06" (with a comment explaining it was deliberately raised above the vault's own 5% idle floor). As written this assertion is false on both sides and the test would fail, meaning the author's own 'claims equal code' self-check was not kept in sync with the IDLE_BUFFER bump. The real enforcement at lib.rs:216-221 does correctly use 0.06, so runtime behavior matches the manifest; only the self-verifying test is wrong.

review.summary: The package is a single long-running async agent (FundingBasis) that holds BTC spot long and BTC-PERP short in equal notional, widening the pair when perp funding is attractive and the vault isn't in drawdown, and unwinding it when funding falls or the vault has dropped 10% from its peak. Every event (a venue account update or a vault event) triggers one `step()`: read fresh state from the venue, decide to open, unwind, or do nothing, and submit at most one paired order per step. Hard caps (gross leverage, per-order size, idle buffer, drawdown stop) are declared as constants in config.rs and threaded through a `Limits` struct into an SDK-provided `size_for` for opening, and into a local `cap_by_notional` for unwinding. A `Halting` vault event triggers a bounded flatten loop that ignores the per-order cap to close out before the vault's own contract-level unwind takes over."
limits: The `shonin-strategy-sdk` crate's implementation (size_for, drivers::submit/account_events/account_state, transfers::move_, vault::events, the Limits/Verdict types) is an external, versioned dependency and was not part of the submitted source, so the arithmetic that is actually supposed to enforce MAX_GROSS_LEVERAGE and MAX_ORDER_FRACTION on the opening path could not be read, only inferred from how it is called.

config/drivers.toml, which presumably defines what venue the "local" driver actually resolves to, was not shown, so the real liquidity and manipulability of the BTC / BTC-PERP market this agent trades could not be assessed directly.
The vault contract's own logic (claims, the 5% idle floor it is said never to cross, halting semantics) is referenced only through the vault:: module and was not shown.
This review did not execute the code or its test suite; the stale-test finding above is based on reading the assertion, not on an actual `cargo test` run.
Operational facts such as how often this agent process is actually restarted in production, and therefore how often the peak-reset gap would be exercised, are unknown.
This is one reading of the source, done once, and is not a proof that no other issue exists.
